_comment: Reviewed exceptions to the dependency gate, one entry per package that an
advisory is reported against. An entry is a decision somebody made and
signed, not a mute button: `reviewBy` is enforced, so an exception that
nobody revisits fails the build on its own once the date passes. That is
the difference between a documented risk acceptance an auditor will accept
(SOC 2 CC7.1, ISO 27001 A.8.8) and a disabled control they will not.
Only add an entry when the advisory genuinely cannot be reached in what we
deploy. If it can be reached, fix it.

backend.advisory: Stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs
backend.reason: Reached only through the Prisma CLI's config loader, which runs once at container start to read our own prisma.config and never on a request path. The input is a file we wrote, not anything a user can send. npm's suggested fix is prisma@6.12.0, which is OLDER than the 6.19.3 we run, so taking it would be a downgrade rather than a fix.

Already a devDependency. It is still counted because @prisma/client declares it as a peer, and it is genuinely present in the image because the entrypoint runs `prisma db push` on start. Same reachability argument as deepmerge-ts above.
Transitive carrier of the entry above; no separate defect of its own.
